issues.legal_issue: A marriage that is emotionally and practically dead may be dissolved in the exercise of constitutional power, subject to a condition, even when cruelty was not proved as a statutory ground in the courts below.
material_facts: The spouses had not enjoyed each other’s company as husband and wife for twenty-five years.
The courts below found that serious allegations made by the wife about the husband’s character had not been proved and could not support divorce for cruelty.
The husband had not adequately discharged his responsibilities towards his wife or contributed to raising their child.
The marriage was emotionally and practically dead, and the child of the marriage was grown and in service.
The husband expressed remorse and offered to transfer his only house to his wife.
issues.conclusion: The Court dissolved the marriage in exercise of Article 142, conditional on the husband transferring the house to his wife and handing over possession; the dissolution would take effect upon completion of those conditions.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for divorce on the ground of cruelty. V. Bhagat v. D. Bhagat (Mrs.) explained the concept of mental and physical cruelty under that provision. Chanderkala Trivedi (Smt.) v. Dr. S.P. Trivedi held that where a marriage is dead and has no chance of being retrieved, it is better to bring it to an end. Applying that principle to the circumstances here, the Court used its power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to dissolve the marriage despite the lower courts’ finding that the alleged cruelty had not been proved.

rule.if: matrimonial_appeal and statutory_cruelty_not_proved and marriage_emotionally_and_practically_dead and spouses_lacked_marital_company_for_long_period and husband_failed_marital_and_parental_responsibilities and child_is_grown_and_independent and husband_expressed_remorse_and_offered_house_transfer

predicates.matrimonial_appeal: A party brought an appeal concerning the continuation or dissolution of a marriage.
predicates.statutory_cruelty_not_proved: The courts below found that the alleged conduct relied on as cruelty had not been proved.
predicates.marriage_emotionally_and_practically_dea: The court found that the marriage had ceased to exist in an emotional and practical sense.
predicates.spouses_lacked_marital_company_for_long_: The spouses had not enjoyed each other’s company as husband and wife for a long period.
predicates.husband_failed_marital_and_parental_resp: The husband had not adequately fulfilled his responsibilities towards his wife or contributed to raising their child.
predicates.child_is_grown_and_independent: The child of the marriage had grown up and was in service.
predicates.husband_expressed_remorse_and_offered_ho: The husband expressed remorse for his conduct and offered to transfer his only house to his wife.

issues.definition: When a matrimonial appeal concerns a marriage that is emotionally and practically dead after a long absence of marital company, and the other stated circumstances are present, the marriage may be dissolved subject to the offered house transfer and delivery of possession.
